finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST parameter 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents(), which fetches arbitrary URLs (http, https, ftp, file://, php://, and others). An attacker can reach internal services and cloud metadata, and read local files. The response length is echoed back, giving a blind oracle for the fetch.

trace.note: Branch entered on any POST request with a 'feed' parameter. No require_admin() call on this path.
$_POST['feed'] is passed unmodified to file_get_contents(), which makes the server-side request or reads the local file.
strlen($xml) is returned to the caller, so a blind SSRF can be probed by response size.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP or DNS check, and no authentication. require_admin() is defined at line 4 but is not called before this sink. Nothing disables wrappers. The webhook branch at lines 17-25 (curl_init($_POST['set_webhook'])) is also an unvalidated sink, but it is gated by require_admin(), which exits with 403 for non-admins, so I did not report it as a separate finding.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] unmodified to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen, with no auth check (require_admin() at line 4 is only called at line 18 in the webhook branch) and no scheme or host validation.
